name: unhcr-refugee-data-finder

task.question: The UNHCR asylum-applications distribution has just been refreshed to carry complete data for year D. For an asylum corridor (country of origin O, country of asylum H) whose government-procedure applications in year D are at least 500 and whose year-D-1 value is published, will the corridor's year-D+1 government-procedure application total reach at least twice the year-D total?
task.prediction_time: The publication instant of the UNHCR asylum-applications annual data for year D on the machine-fetchable HDX channel: an observed refresh cycle (2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22, 2026-08-20) whose 2026-08-20 refresh carries complete data through year 2025 (max Year = 2025 measured on the fetched bytes), 232 days after the 2025 period end; UNHCR's Global Trends cycle lands mid-D+1. At that instant every feature is a corridor-year total for years <= D. The target year D+1 has partially elapsed at the instant but its value is entirely unpublished on this channel (first available ~mid D+2), so this is an annual publication-lag nowcast, not a future-event forecast.

event_key_note: surge_cluster = origin|label-year: one displacement event hits many corridors in one year (SYR->many hosts 2015), so the conservative independent-event count is the distinct (origin, label-year) pair among positives
feature_documentation: every shipped feature is a corridor-year or context total for published years <= D, or a corridor/calendar identity: origin and asylum are the publisher's ISO-3-style codes; target_year is the label year's calendar identity; apps_d/apps_d1 are the corridor's government-procedure persons totals for years D and D-1 (the year-D value is the doubling baseline, published at the instant); log_growth_d is ln(apps_d+1)-ln(apps_d1+1); surged_recently flags apps_d >= 2*apps_d1 (the corridor already doubled into D); host_apps_d/host_growth_d and origin_apps_d/origin_growth_d are the same-year host-country and origin-country all-corridor totals and their log growth (reception-capacity and displacement-pressure context); corridor_age is years since the corridor first appears in the fetched panel. The year-D+1 value (the label operand) and every year > D value are excluded from the shipped columns. target_date is December 31 of the label year - a calendar identifier derived from target_year, not a publication timestamp (the prediction instant is the HDX refresh publication; see timing); surge_cluster is the origin|label-year surge-event grouping used for clustered counting. Both are runner-visible inputs and are declared in the feature inventory.
high_cardinality_note: row_id is unique per row and surge_cluster (origin|label-year) carries more levels than rows/5 in the narrower splits; both are declared rather than scored, and their information is fully recoverable from origin, asylum and target_year
label_source_columns: year-D+1 corridor G/P total (source column 'Number of Applications' at Year=D+1, all application types summed)

measurements.frame: corridor government-procedure persons applications in year D, summed over all application types, current-vintage
the same corridor total for year D-1
ln(apps_d+1) - ln(apps_d1+1), the observed momentum at D
apps_d >= 2 x apps_d1, the corridor's own last-step doubling observed at D
all-corridor government-procedure total received by the host country in year D
ln(host total D + 1) - ln(host total D-1 + 1)
all-host government-procedure total from the origin country in year D
ln(origin total D + 1) - ln(origin total D-1 + 1)
D minus the corridor's first year in the fetched panel (>= 1 by the eligibility rule)

measurements.unit: ISO date (year-end of the label year)
measurements.frame: calendar identity of the outcome window; used as the split time column
event key for clustered positive counting
1 iff year-D+1 corridor total >= 2 x year-D total; a missing corridor row with the host still reporting counts as 0 applications

known_event.name: 2015 Syrian surge into Germany (SYR->DEU 2014->2015)
known_event.detail: 41,100 -> 162,510, x2 label TRUE - asserted in-build with the AFG->USA 2021->2022 TRUE and AFG->DEU 2021->2022 FALSE fixtures and the UKR->POL below-eligibility case
known_event.source: UNHCR asylum statistics via HDX (the fetched panel itself; values verified at discovery against the publisher's own interactive Data Finder)

prediction_instant.citation: HDX resource update history observed 2026-10-23: refreshes 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22 and 2026-08-20; the 2026-08-20 refresh carries complete data through year 2025 (max Year = 2025 measured on the fetched bytes, 232 days after the 2025 period end); UNHCR's Global Trends cycle lands mid-D+1

row_selection.latest_period_used: Y (year D, the last fully published year)
row_selection.basis: eligibility reads only published years <= D: the corridor's year-D government-procedure total >= 500 and a published year-D-1 corridor value. Label-observability censoring excludes corridors whose host files no G/P report at all in D+1 (label undefined, never counted as zero) and live-edge label years beyond the fetched vintage; both are counted per split in summary.json and never condition on the label value. The target year D+1 never enters eligibility.

split_boundaries.train: label years 2002-2016 shipped (window start 2001-01-01, end exclusive; label-year 2001 contributes no rows: the panel starts 2000 so no corridor has a published 1999 value - counted in summary.json)
split_boundaries.holdout: label years 2022-2025 (window end exclusive; through the last year the fetched vintage carries; 2025 on the pinned snapshot)

positive_events_note: positives and distinct (origin, label-year) surge clusters per split, recomputed from the written rows; the gate re-verifies
id_columns_note: row_id = origin-asylum-labelyear names one corridor-year with one label; the corridor itself recurs across label years by design (a panel task), which is why the corridor pair ships as features and only row_id is the identifier

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is a corridor-year whose features read published years <= D only. Honest evaluation requires isolated rows - one row presented to the solver at a time - because the panel is self-answering across adjacent label years (see the declared cross-row probe). The shipped illustrative runner does NOT enforce this: it passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor in one call, and the independent pre-flip audit (2026-10-28) measured frozen label-blind recoveries from that access (eval AUC 0.9753 from eval features alone, holdout AUC 0.9830, 0.9970 across all splits, plus exact count recovery from next-year apps_d), so scores under unrestricted access are meaningless. Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: HDX distributes one in-place-revised resource with no historical vintages, so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed and the artifact is retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup.

row_id.availability: identity of the row; corridor and label year are both known at the instant

origin.availability: publisher-assigned corridor identity, constant across the panel

asylum.availability: publisher-assigned corridor identity, constant across the panel

target_year.availability: calendar arithmetic on the instant's last published year

apps_d.source: sum of 'Number of Applications' over G/P application-type rows at Year D
apps_d.availability: the year-D refresh is the instant itself (observed 2026-08-20 carrying complete data through 2025)
apps_d.assumption: current-vintage value; the value published at past instants is unverifiable (no historical vintages)

apps_d1.source: the same summed panel at Year D-1
apps_d1.availability: published one refresh before the instant, so available at it

log_growth_d.source: deterministic function of apps_d and apps_d1
log_growth_d.availability: derivable at the instant from published years <= D

surged_recently.source: deterministic flag on apps_d >= 2 x apps_d1

host_apps_d.source: all-corridor sum of the same G/P stream at (Year D, asylum)
host_apps_d.availability: published at the instant (same refresh as apps_d)

host_growth_d.source: deterministic function of host totals at D and D-1

origin_apps_d.source: all-host sum of the same G/P stream at (Year D, origin)

origin_growth_d.source: deterministic function of origin totals at D and D-1

corridor_age.source: D minus the corridor's first year in the fetched panel
corridor_age.availability: derivable at the instant from published years <= D
corridor_age.assumption: panel start 2000 truncates true corridor age for pre-2000 corridors; age is 'years since first observed in the fetched panel'

target_date.source: calendar year-end of the label year
target_date.availability: calendar arithmetic; the carry column is the split time column, not an observation

surge_cluster.availability: identity of the row's cluster; both parts known at the instant

vintage.evidence: HDX distributes one in-place-revised resource: the record observed refreshes 2025-11-05, 2026-02-25, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-22, 2026-08-20 and no archived vintages are retained, so a reverse-history probe is not performable on this channel. The fetched snapshot is pinned by sha256 and the build asserts the recorded known-event fixtures against it; values are construction-time current-vintage and no historical point-in-time availability is claimed. Same documented posture as abs-visitor-arrivals-direction.

selection.evidence: eligibility reads only published years <= D (year-D corridor total >= 500 and a published year-D-1 value). Label-observability censoring - host files no G/P report at all in D+1, or the label year lies beyond the fetched vintage - excludes rows whose label is undefined and counts them per split in summary.json; it never conditions on the label value and never decides another row's membership (the same pending-censored pattern the accepted ec-merger-phase2-opening artifact uses)

limitations: Annual grain only on the machine-fetchable channel; a monthly variant would need the WAF-gated UNHCR Data Finder app or an operator decision on browser-captured exports.
Current-vintage panel with no historical vintages: this is retrospective research, not certified historical forecasting; intra-basis revision size is unmeasurable without archived vintages.

The prediction instant lies inside the target year (publication-lag nowcast): the target year has partially elapsed at the instant; what is claimed is value-unavailability on this channel, not that the window follows the instant.

Temporary-protection registrations (Ukrainians in the EU from 2022) are not asylum applications and do not enter the stream - the 2022 Ukraine displacement is largely absent from this task by construction (UKR->POL fixture).
Prevalence drifts across splits (more surges in later years; recorded 8.2% train / 8.7% eval / 11.7% holdout before the year-D-1 refinement) - a property of the period, reported beside every score.
Positives cluster by (origin, label-year) surge events beyond the row count; clustered counts are reported beside every score.

377 rows (4.9% of eligible corridor-years on the pinned snapshot) lack a published year-D-1 value and are excluded with per-split counts (314 train - 192 panel-start label-year-2001 rows plus 122 with no published year-D-1 cell; 31 eval; 32 holdout; mostly label-year 2001, where the panel start makes every prior year unpublished).
Unsplit-V application-type rows live mostly in the training era (1,238 of 3,677 recorded train rows); the sum-across-types rule is what the BAMF cross-check validates.
Corridor age is measured from the fetched panel's 2000 start, truncating true age for older corridors.

probes.name: next_label_year_exposes_outcome
probes.expectation: the donor row (same corridor, label year T+1) carries surged_recently = (year-T total >= 2 x year-T-1 total), which is exactly the earlier row's label: a panel is self-answering across rows one year apart. Coverage therefore measures the cross-row outcome exposure inherent to the task; the isolated-rows protocol is the required mitigation for honest evaluation, declared here as a requirement - the shipped illustrative runner does not enforce it, and the independent pre-flip audit (2026-10-28) measured the unrestricted recoveries (eval AUC 0.975325, holdout 0.983034, 0.996970 across all splits)

cross_row_audit.rationale: rows are corridor-years on a self-answering panel: a row with label year T+1 ships the year-T corridor total as apps_d, which is the label operand of the row with label year T. The probe measures that exposure from the artifact itself on every full configuration (train, eval, holdout); covered rows make this restricted retrospective research under a protocol that any honest evaluation must enforce and that nothing in this package enforces, and no historical forecasting claim is made.
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the extract ships exactly the runner layout - public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json, quality.json; the fetched source CSV, the panel and all diagnostics stay outside the artifact; no joint label matrices or other solver-visible files exist in the dataset directory
cross_row_audit.reverse_history: not performable: HDX retains no archived vintages of this resource (observed in-place revision 2025-11-05 through 2026-08-20), so no as-of reconstruction can be probed; the current-vintage posture above is the recorded consequence
